$comment: Explicit, reviewed allowlist of print_ids whose own verify recomputation is EXPECTED to diverge from their published figures, and why — read by cli/verify-all.ts. Never auto-derived from a heuristic (e.g. 'this print has some correction_notes'): every entry here is added by hand alongside the correction_notes entry that discloses and quantifies the same divergence, so this file stays a small, honest, human-reviewed record rather than a way to silence a genuinely new failure. A print's own body is never edited to fix these — see docs/methodology.md's revision policy. Found live 2026-09-26: cli/verify.ts's real recompute (once its own rounding-rule bug — passing print.rounding, not always today's default — was fixed) showed 22 published prints diverging from current-code recomputation, every one of them already fully or structurally disclosed via that print's own correction_notes; none was a previously-unknown, undisclosed error.

Recomputing today (current registry, missing both) naturally shows them as "model absent from recomputation" rather than "excluded". See 2026-08-30's own retroactive correction note for the full disclosure. A benign, real registry change, not a computation error on either side.
